# HTML documents

- All HTML documents must start with a document type declaration: `<!DOCTYPE html>`.
- The HTML document itself begins with `<html>` and ends with `</html>`.
- The visible part of the HTML is between `<body>` and `</body>`.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="es">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Page title</title>
</head>
<body>
    <h1>My first heading</h1>
    <p>My first paragraph</p>
</body>
</html>
```

# The `<!DOCTYPE>` declaration

- The `<!DOCTYPE>` declaration represents the document type and helps browserss to display web pages correctly.
- It must only appear once at the top of the page before any HTML tags
- The `<!DOCTYPE>` declaration is not case sensitive
- The `<!DOCTYPE>` declaration for HTML is:

> `<!DOCTYPE html>`

# HTML headings

- HTML headings are defined with `<h1>` to `<h6>` tags.
- `<h1>` defines the most important heading
- `<h6>` defines the least important heading

# HTML paragraphs

- HTML paragraphs are defined with `<p>` tag

# HTML links

HTML links are defined with the `<a>` tag:

- The link's destination is specified in the `href` attribute.
- Attributes are used to provide additional information about HTML elements.

# HTML images

HTML images are defined with `<img>` tag:

- The source file (`scr`), alternative text (`alt`), `width` and `height` are provided as attributes.
- `alt` stands for **Alternative Text** where it provides a text description of the image for 3 critical reasons:

  - Accesibility for visually impaired users
  - The browser will dsiplay the `alt` text in place of a broken image box
  - Search engine bots rely heavily on `alt` text to understand what the image contains and index it properly in search results
